insights.title: Section mean gap between Section A and Section B
insights.detail: Section A averages 24.30 (leniency index 1.23) against 16.50 in Section B (leniency index 0.79) — a gap of 7.80 marks on the same assessment. Identical cohorts should not diverge this far.

insights.title: Section A sits above the cohort mean
insights.detail: Section A (n=20, instructor Prof. Monir) has a z-score of 0.60 against the cohort, with standard deviation 1.60 and skewness -0.38.

insights.title: Section B sits below the cohort mean
insights.detail: Section B (n=20, instructor Dr. Hasan) has a z-score of -0.60 against the cohort, with standard deviation 7.30 and skewness 0.38.

insights.title: Unequal spread between sections
insights.detail: The wider section varies 4.56x more than the tighter one, so the two graders are not only differing on average but on how far they spread marks.

insights.title: Proposed normalisation
insights.detail: A shift of +4.5 marks on Section B realigns it with the cohort mean while preserving within-section rank order.

normalization.rationale: Applying a +4.5 mark normalisation shift to Section B realigns the section mean with cohort expectations based on student coursework baseline, mitigating grader disparity while preserving rank order.

ai_summary: Grading drift detected: Section A averages 24.30 marks against 16.50 in Section B on the same assessment, a leniency spread of 1.23 versus 0.79. A +4.5 mark normalisation on Section B is proposed.
